meta.title: Practice — Atelier Nero
meta.description: The practice, method, timeline, and thinking behind Atelier Nero.

data.body: Atelier Nero was established in Rome in 2014 by architects Elisa Marconi and Davide Serra. The studio works where architecture meets movement, display, and institutional clarity: residences, galleries, cultural interiors, public programs, and signage systems. We prefer exact language, durable materials, and spatial sequences that remain intelligible without explanation.

image.alt: Monumental concrete facade with rhythmic openings

data.label: Practice
data.title: Architecture as a system of clear decisions

data.intro: The studio has moved from residential interiors to public commissions and exhibition infrastructure without changing its disciplinary core.

items.body: Initial work focused on residential alterations, artist studios, and bespoke interior systems.
items.title: Practice founded in Rome

items.body: A navigation system for a civic archive introduced the studio to public-facing cultural infrastructure.
items.title: First institutional wayfinding commission

items.body: Temporary and long-duration exhibitions in Switzerland and Germany extended the studio’s work into logistics, visitor flow, and display architecture.
items.title: Exhibition design expands internationally

items.body: Current commissions often combine shell architecture, interiors, furnishings, and wayfinding into a single spatial language.
items.title: Integrated architecture and signage work

data.label: Timeline
data.title: A practice built through sequential scales

data.intro: We maintain a small, senior-led structure. Drawings remain close to design thinking. Technical detail is developed early, not deferred.

items.body: Every commission is led directly by the partners and reviewed through iterative drawing, model, and site dialogue.
items.title: Senior authorship

items.body: Consultant alignment, technical packages, and material tolerances are treated as design work, not administration.
items.title: Hard coordination

items.body: We use concise documentation, controlled detailing, and clear decision gates to keep projects legible for clients and contractors.
items.title: Exact communication

items.body: No formal move enters the project unless it clarifies use, hierarchy, or experience.
items.title: Purposeful restraint
